questions.question: 1. A BERT encoder is pretrained with masked language modelling on '[CLS]1 the2 technician3 [MASK]4 the5 faulty6 [MASK]7 quickly8 [SEP]9'. Which context is available when computing output at position 4, and how many loss terms does this instance contribute?
options: All other positions; nine loss terms
All other positions; two loss terms
questions.correctAnswer: All other positions; two loss terms
questions.explanation: BERT self-attention is bidirectional without causal masking, so position 4 attends to all other positions. Only masked positions (4 and 7) contribute loss terms, so 2 loss terms.

questions.question: 2. A span-based model processes an input sequence of T = 12 tokens. A span runs from start i to end j with 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ T, with length limit L = 4 (j − i < L). How many legal spans does the model enumerate?
questions.explanation: Lengths l in {1, 2, 3, 4}. Number of spans of length l is T - l + 1: l=1: 12, l=2: 11, l=3: 10, l=4: 9. Sum = 12 + 11 + 10 + 9 = 42.

questions.question: 3. A BERT-based reading comprehension model uses start vector S = [1, 1] and end vector E = [1, −1]. Final representations: T1=[6, 2], T2=[2, 0], T3=[3, −3], T4=[3, −1], T5=[5, −1], T6=[3, −5]. Span score is S·Ti + E·Tj with j ≥ i and j − i < 3. Which span is predicted and its score?
questions.explanation: Start scores: s1=8, s2=2, s3=0, s4=2, s5=4, s6=-2. End scores: e1=4, e2=2, e3=6, e4=4, e5=6, e6=8. Under j ≥ i and j - i ≤ 2: span (1, 3) gives s1 + e3 = 8 + 6 = 14, which is the maximum legal score.

questions.question: 4. A single T5 model is fine-tuned for two tasks: judging grammatical acceptability (2-way decision) and rating sentence pair similarity (1–5 scale). Under the text-to-text framework, how are the two outputs produced?
options: Classification as text; score by regression
Both are generated as literal text
questions.correctAnswer: Both are generated as literal text
questions.explanation: In T5's text-to-text framework, both classification decisions (e.g. 'not acceptable') and continuous scores (e.g. '3.8') are emitted directly as literal text tokens by the decoder.

questions.question: 5. A decoder-only Transformer is pretrained on w1 w2 w3 w4 w5. Conditional probabilities: p(w2|w1)=0.5, p(w3|w1w2)=0.25, p(w4|w1..w3)=0.5, p(w5|w1..w4)=0.125. Using log2(0.5)=-1, log2(0.25)=-2, log2(0.125)=-3, what is the total negative log-likelihood of the tokens predicted by this pretraining objective?
questions.explanation: w1 is context-only and not predicted. The 4 predicted tokens have -log2 values: 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 7.

questions.question: 6. A team continues pretraining RoBERTa on appliance e-manuals. In-domain QA improves substantially, but average GLUE score falls below the original checkpoint. Which diagnosis and remedy apply?
options: Catastrophic forgetting; replace the model vocabulary
Catastrophic forgetting; mix general pretraining data
Overfitting to GLUE; use early stopping
Curse of multilinguality; use temperature sampling
questions.correctAnswer: Catastrophic forgetting; mix general pretraining data
questions.explanation: Continued training on narrow in-domain data causes catastrophic forgetting of general domain capabilities. The remedy is rehearsal: mixing general pretraining data into continued pretraining.

questions.question: 7. A 2-layer biLM produces ELMo representations with weights s0=0.1, s1=0.5, s2=0.4 and scale factor γ=2. xk=[1, 0]; h1=[2, 1, 0, 3]; h2=[1, 4, 2, 0]. What is ELMo_k?
